stem: Two rooms deliver similar daily light integral but use substantially different day lengths. Which conclusion is best supported?
choices: Similar DLI does not guarantee equivalent flowering signals because photoperiod and total photon dose are different biological variables
Similar DLI usually means the developmental light signal is comparable because total daily photon delivery is the dominant cue in flowering
The room with higher instantaneous intensity should have the stronger flowering signal even if its day length is shorter
Dark-period timing matters mainly for total photon accounting, so matching DLI is generally enough to compare reproductive light responses
rationale: Photoperiod is developmental information based on recurring light-dark timing, whereas DLI summarizes total daily photon delivery. They are related through time but are not interchangeable.
